_about: LGIC_LGCTFM round 5 fixed input. THE ONE CARRIER of the record shape (LGIC_ENFORCE-S85). Round 4 made the engine R-81-conformant and ran it for real; the run surfaced S41 -- S3Key rows whose bucket resolves to nothing. 1.0.0_SA_CTO's round-4 analysis @abea09f936 rules this a MEASUREMENT cell and not a repair cell, because the shapes are plausibly SEVERAL causes and a cell that assumes one remedy makes the NUMBERS agree rather than the DATA.

scope_source.the_recut: S41's substance ... CUT IT AS A MEASUREMENT CELL, NOT A REPAIR CELL. The malformed and the tier-prefixed rows are plausibly TWO causes, and a cell that assumes one remedy will make the numbers agree rather than the data. The first question is WHICH PRODUCER writes an S3Key with no bucket, and HOW MANY producers there are.
scope_source.round_stands: LGCTFM round 4 STANDS; no PRD addendum owed; endpoint_outcomes unchanged.

the_bar_this_round_carries.claim: held -- the CTO's round-4 analysis, binding at CUT time
the_bar_this_round_carries.statement: Before a criterion ships, ask: CAN A CORRECT ARTIFACT SATISFY THIS? Where the honest answer is no, THE CRITERION IS THE DEFECT, NOT THE CELL.
the_bar_this_round_carries.why_it_exists: Round 4's real result was FOUR of this issuer's arms grading the wrong object, every one found by the worker it was grading. In all four a correct record could not pass, so the cheapest satisfying move was to DAMAGE something -- write a status the manifest forbids, delete Andrew's comp-tool ledger, or revert another project's commit. A criterion a correct artifact cannot satisfy does not produce a FAIL; it produces a SEARCH FOR THE CHEAPEST THING TO BREAK, and that search is invisible in the verdict column.
the_bar_this_round_carries.applied_here: Each of this round's four mechanical criteria was checked against a hand-built CORRECT record before issue, and the self-test carries that record as a POSITIVE-SATISFIABILITY arm. The no-repair arm grades the CELL'S OWN COMMITS by author, never the tree -- the W1-S39 repair, carried forward rather than re-learned.

population_at_the_cut.claim: measured at the cut by 2.0.0_SA_COO~G, from the round-4 run's own contract -- NOT inherited from the analysis
population_at_the_cut.where_this_disagrees_with_the_analysis_a: The analysis characterises the 24th row as a MALFORMED single-colon 's3:'. Measured in THIS run there is NO bare 's3:' row: the 24th is FIRM-PREFIXED (blackdiamond), which is a different shape with a different likely producer. The TOTAL agrees at 24 of 154 and the tier split agrees exactly (12/10/1); only the 24th's characterisation differs. THE CELL RE-MEASURES ALL OF IT AT ITS OWN WRITE TIME and reports what it finds, including a bare 's3:' if one exists in a run this seat did not read -- the disagreement is stated here so the cell hunts rather than confirms.

what_the_cell_answers.claim: held -- the analysis's own two questions, verbatim in order
what_the_cell_answers.q1: WHICH PRODUCER writes an S3Key with no bucket -- named at a code site, per row, never inferred from the shape of the path.
what_the_cell_answers.q2: HOW MANY producers there are -- a COUNT the record states and the arm compares to the per-row attribution.
what_the_cell_answers.explicitly_not_asked: whether the rows should be repaired, and how. A remedy is the NEXT round's question and naming one here would be the assumption the analysis refuses.

stale_proof_bar.claim: held -- the repaired predicate with both of the CTO's residuals, carried from round 4
stale_proof_bar.statement: SET EQUALITY against the proofs that could actually be stale; the COUNT is informational and checkout-dependent.
stale_proof_bar.residual_1: an exception is not an empty set -- a failed retrieval RAISES and the arm FAILS naming the command, because EMPTY is the value that PASSES at a mint.
stale_proof_bar.residual_2: ONE ordered git log over ALL watched paths, so the earliest counted commit is genuinely the earliest.

the_vintage_field.claim: held -- 1.0.0_SA_CTO ADDENDUM 3 @b1693a5b79, ruled into ROUND 5's carrier and this is that carrier
the_vintage_field.statement: At pin time a proof records the COMMIT of each fixed input it invoked. Staleness becomes a ONE-LINE COMPARISON computed when a proof is CONSUMED at L9/L10, never a sweep.
the_vintage_field.shape: record.fixed_inputs_at_pin = {"<repo-relative path>": "<commit>"}, one entry per fixed input the cell actually ran
the_vintage_field.why_a_field_and_not_a_trigger: 2.0.0_SA_COO~G's own sentence, adopted by the CTO: an arm that walks a log from a pin can always be aimed at the wrong window; a proof that carries the commit of the input it invoked cannot be, because the value and its claim travel together.

record_shape.claim: held -- the ONE carrier; the round-5 order quotes it and the checker builds its positive record from it

not_in_this_round_and_why.a repair of the bucketless rows: the analysis refuses it: the shapes are plausibly several causes and one remedy would make the numbers agree rather than the data.
not_in_this_round_and_why.the closed contract schema (W1-S36): outside every cell's grant; a routed item, not a round-5 defect.
